\section[l'avvenimento]{l'avvenimento — the event, the happening}

\label{lesson:IT-C276-avvenimento}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to take place, then the Italian for what happened.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: l'avvenimento}
\textbf{l'avvenimento} — \textquotedblleft{}the event, the happening\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Il concerto è stato l'avvenimento dell'estate.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The concert was the event of the summer.}
\end{quote}

An important happening. Built on \emph{avvenire}, ‘to take place’.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{avvenimento} is built on \emph{avvenire} \textquotedblleft{}to take place\textquotedblright{}, from Latin \emph{advenīre} \textquotedblleft{}to come to\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), with the noun ending \emph{-mento}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{l'avvenimento}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{l'avvenimento}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{l'avvenimento}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for to take place, then the Italian for what happened, then say \emph{l'avvenimento} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does l'avvenimento mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The event, the happening\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[la vicenda]{la vicenda — the affair, the chain of events}

\label{lesson:IT-C276-vicenda}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for what happened, then the Italian for the event.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la vicenda}
\textbf{la vicenda} — \textquotedblleft{}the affair, the chain of events\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
È una vicenda strana: nessuno sa la verità.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{It is a strange affair: nobody knows the truth.}
\end{quote}

\emph{A vicenda} means ‘in turn, each other’: \emph{si aiutano a vicenda}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{vicenda} is traced in EtymDB to Latin \emph{vicis} \textquotedblleft{}change, turn, alternation\textquotedblright{}: a story is a chain of turns.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la vicenda}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la vicenda}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la vicenda}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for what happened, then the Italian for the event, then say \emph{la vicenda} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does la vicenda mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The affair, the chain of events\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[la faccenda]{la faccenda — the matter, the business; a chore}

\label{lesson:IT-C276-faccenda}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the event, then the Italian for the affair.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la faccenda}
\textbf{la faccenda} — \textquotedblleft{}the matter, the business; a chore\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
È una faccenda complicata.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{It is a complicated matter.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Le faccende di casa} are the housework.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{faccenda} is inherited from Latin \emph{facienda} \textquotedblleft{}things to be done\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{facere} \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[la cronologia]{la cronologia — the chronology, the order of events; browsing history}

\label{lesson:IT-C276-cronologia}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the affair, then the Italian for the matter.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la cronologia}
\textbf{la cronologia} — \textquotedblleft{}the chronology, the order of events; browsing history\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Facciamo la cronologia dei fatti.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Let us put together the chronology of the facts.}
\end{quote}

On a phone or a computer, \emph{la cronologia} is the browsing history.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{cronologia} is a learned word built from Greek \emph{khrónos} \textquotedblleft{}time\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB) and \emph{-logía} \textquotedblleft{}a reckoning, a study\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[la sequenza]{la sequenza — the sequence, the series}

\label{lesson:IT-C276-sequenza}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the matter, then the Italian for the chronology.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la sequenza}
\textbf{la sequenza} — \textquotedblleft{}the sequence, the series\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ricordo bene la sequenza dei fatti.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I remember the sequence of events well.}
\end{quote}

Also a film word: \emph{la prima sequenza del film}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{sequenza} is a learned borrowing from Late Latin \emph{sequentia} \textquotedblleft{}a following\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from \emph{sequī} \textquotedblleft{}to follow\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
